bg.surface.use: panes, cards, the HUD pill: the layer content sits on

bg.raised.use: inputs and secondary buttons at rest

bg.hover.use: a hovered control, row or list item

bg.selected.use: a selected row, list item or nav tab; the info banner

bg.warning.use: warning banner and low-confidence badge fill

bg.danger.use: error banner fill, a hovered destructive button

border.strong.use: control outlines, focused containers, the HUD outline

accent.primary.use: primary buttons, links, focus ring, selection

text.on-accent.use: text on accent.primary (primary buttons); dark theme uses dark text on the bright accent

contrast._note:
Every key in `color` must appear in text, backgrounds, indicators, structural, or in a `pairs` entry: ContrastTests enforces that, so a new token cannot be added without deciding what it is allowed to do.
  text: held to `minimum` against every background.
  backgrounds: every surface text or an indicator is ever drawn on, tints included (v0.5: hover, pressed, selected and the three banner fills), so a tint that dims the words fails here.
  indicators: held to `indicator_minimum`, WCAG's non-text bar, because Spec v0.4.2 confines them to a rule, a border, a dot or a glyph and never to body-size text.
  structural: dividers and container outlines. Held only to being a different colour from the background, not to 3:1. WCAG 1.4.11 applies to visuals that are the sole means of identifying a component or its state, and these are not: a control is identified by its own surface colour and its label, and the focus ring is accent.primary, which is in `text` and so held to 4.5:1.
  pairs: a colour that only ever meets one specific other. text.on-accent is unreadable on anything but the accent, and accent.primary.hover is never a surface for anything else, so they are checked against each other rather than against every background.
